do.name: Walk the national park trails
do.detail: Marked routes run through oak and yew woods and around Muckross Lake, from easy loops to the Old Kenmare Road across open bog.

do.name: Muckross House, gardens and working farms
do.detail: A Victorian mansion with gardens, plus farms run as they were in the 1920s and craft workshops for pottery, weaving and bookbinding.

do.name: Ross Castle on Lough Leane
do.detail: A 15th century tower house two kilometres from town, shown by small guided tours, with lakeshore paths and bike tracks around it.

do.name: Boat across the lakes, walking the Gap of Dunloe
do.detail: The classic day pairs a hike through the mountain gap with an open boat back through the three lakes, landing at Ross Castle.

do.name: Ride a jaunting car
do.detail: Horse drawn traps seating four run from town out to Ross Castle and Muckross, with the driver keeping up a running commentary.

do.name: Torc Waterfall and the Cardiac Steps
do.detail: The fall is five minutes from the car park. Behind it a long stair climbs to a viewpoint over the lakes for those who keep going.

do.name: Hire a bike for the park roads
do.detail: Rental shops sit in town and the traffic free lanes to Ross Castle and Muckross make an easy half day on two wheels.

do.name: Muckross Abbey
do.detail: A Franciscan friary of 1448, roofless but standing, with a yew tree filling the whole cloister.

do.name: Drive the Ring of Kerry
do.detail: A 179 km loop of the Iveragh peninsula, the classic Irish coast drive, and Killarney is where it starts and ends.

do.name: Killarney Races
do.detail: The town racecourse runs meetings from spring to autumn, mixing flat cards with jumps, and the pubs fill up on race evenings.
